split_reasoning: Design, construction, and maintenance produce different work products at different stages of a website's life.

parts.text: Design a website or a defined website feature.
parts.type_reasoning: The design is a distinct artifact used by the development team.
parts.unit_reasoning: A design for a defined feature or site is handed over as a whole.
parts.start: design requirements or brief received
parts.end: design delivered for review or implementation

parts.text: Build a website or a defined website feature using development and content tools.
parts.type_reasoning: Each implementation produces a distinct website component for review or release.
parts.unit_reasoning: A feature or component is a manageable development handoff rather than an entire project.
parts.work_item: one implemented website feature or component
parts.start: feature requirements or design ready for implementation
parts.end: component submitted for review or deployment

parts.text: Maintain an existing website by making a requested change or correction.
parts.type_reasoning: Each maintenance change produces an updated site component.
parts.unit_reasoning: A requested change or correction is normally tracked and completed as a unit.
parts.start: maintenance request or defect identified
parts.end: change completed and submitted for release

notes: Shares are approximate and vary with the site's development stage.

split_reasoning: Performing updates and directing other people to perform them are different activities.

parts.text: Perform a website update.
parts.type_reasoning: An update produces a distinct change to the site.
parts.unit_reasoning: A requested update is the unit reviewed and released.
parts.start: update request or approved change received
parts.end: update completed and submitted for release

parts.text: Direct staff performing website updates.
parts.type_reasoning: Directing staff is supervisory interaction rather than a distinct update produced by the worker.

notes: The split depends on the worker's supervisory responsibilities.

split_reasoning: Prioritizing needs, resolving conflicts, and choosing criteria or solutions are purposes of the same kind of team discussion.

parts.text: Confer with management or development teams about priorities, conflicts, content criteria, or solutions.
parts.type_reasoning: The work is a live discussion and coordination with colleagues.

split_reasoning: Backing up website files is one activity with a single kind of output.

parts.text: Back up website files to a local directory for recovery.
parts.type_reasoning: Each backup produces a recoverable copy relied on by the site team.
parts.unit_reasoning: A backup run for a site or defined file set is a checkable unit.
parts.start: scheduled or requested backup is due
parts.end: files copied to the local backup location and completion checked

split_reasoning: Validity, structure, standards, and compatibility are criteria applied in the same code evaluation.

parts.text: Evaluate website or application code against structural, standards, and compatibility requirements.
parts.type_reasoning: Each evaluation produces review findings or an approval for a code change.
parts.unit_reasoning: A code change or defined code submission is reviewed as a unit.
parts.start: code submitted for evaluation
parts.end: findings or approval returned to the developer

split_reasoning: Education, reading, and professional events are alternative means of staying current.

parts.text: Keep current with web technologies and programming practices.
parts.type_reasoning: The target describes maintaining knowledge rather than producing a specific item for others.

split_reasoning: Analyzing needs and determining requirements form one requirements-definition activity.

parts.text: Analyze user needs and define technical requirements.
parts.type_reasoning: The analysis produces requirements used by the development team.
parts.unit_reasoning: A defined feature or request yields a requirements set that can be reviewed as a whole.
parts.work_item: one set of technical requirements for a defined need
parts.start: user need or project request received
parts.end: requirements recorded and shared for review
parts.checked_by: users, project stakeholders, and development team

split_reasoning: Developing a supporting database is one implementation activity.

parts.text: Develop a database or database component supporting a website or web application.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a database implementation for application developers to use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A defined database component or schema change is a reviewable development unit.
parts.work_item: one implemented database component or schema change
parts.start: database requirements or change request received
parts.end: database component submitted for review or deployment

split_reasoning: Domain registration renewal is a single administrative activity.

parts.text: Renew a website's domain name registration.
parts.type_reasoning: Each renewal produces a confirmed continuation of a registration.
parts.unit_reasoning: A domain registration is renewed and confirmed as an individual unit.
parts.start: renewal notice or upcoming expiration identified
parts.end: renewal confirmed by the registrar and recorded

split_reasoning: Developing an e-commerce strategy with stakeholders and integrating it into a website are different activities.

parts.text: Collaborate with management or users to develop an e-commerce strategy.
parts.type_reasoning: The target emphasizes collaborative strategy discussions with stakeholders.

parts.text: Integrate an e-commerce strategy into a website.
parts.type_reasoning: Integration produces a website feature or change that stakeholders can review.
parts.unit_reasoning: A defined e-commerce feature or integration is implemented and handed over as a unit.
parts.work_item: one e-commerce website integration or feature
parts.start: strategy and feature requirements agreed
parts.end: integration submitted for review or deployment

notes: The relative shares depend on the worker's strategy and implementation responsibilities.

split_reasoning: Writing supporting code is one activity across websites and web applications.

parts.text: Write supporting code for a website or web application.
parts.type_reasoning: Each coding assignment produces a distinct code change.
parts.unit_reasoning: A code change for a defined requirement is submitted and reviewed as a unit.
parts.start: coding requirement or development task assigned
parts.end: code submitted for review or integration

split_reasoning: Communicating about hardware or software issues is one coordination activity regardless of the recipient.

parts.text: Coordinate with network personnel or hosting agencies about issues affecting a website.
parts.type_reasoning: The work centers on coordination with other parties to address an issue.

notes: Some workplaces also use written support tickets; the target does not specify that output.

split_reasoning: Scheduled tests and tests after revisions are the same activity triggered at different times.

parts.text: Perform a planned or post-revision website test.
parts.type_reasoning: Each test execution produces results that the development team uses.
parts.unit_reasoning: A defined test run is completed and its outcome handed to the team as a unit.
parts.start: scheduled test is due or a revision is ready to test
parts.end: test executed and outcome recorded or reported

notes: Detailed test documentation is separately covered by task 14726.

split_reasoning: Programming languages, design tools, and applications are alternative types of technology selected for development.

parts.text: Select a programming language, design tool, or application for a development need.
parts.type_reasoning: The selection yields a technology choice that the team can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A choice for a defined need is communicated and acted on as a unit.
parts.start: development need and selection criteria identified
parts.end: choice recorded or communicated to the team

split_reasoning: Answering individual inquiries and setting up an automated response system are different activities.

parts.text: Respond to a user inquiry received by email.
parts.type_reasoning: Each email inquiry produces a response sent to the user.
parts.unit_reasoning: An individual inquiry and its reply are handled as one correspondence item.
parts.start: user inquiry received by email
parts.end: response sent to the user
parts.checked_by: the user and, when applicable, a supervisor

parts.text: Set up an automated system to respond to user inquiries.
parts.type_reasoning: The setup produces a configured response mechanism that the site team relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: A defined automated response setup or change is configured and handed over as a unit.
parts.start: response automation requirement identified
parts.end: configuration tested and made available for use

notes: Time shares vary with the volume of inquiries and frequency of automation changes.

split_reasoning: Developing a revision procedure and implementing it are different activities with different outputs.

parts.text: Develop a procedure for ongoing website revision.
parts.type_reasoning: The procedure is a documented process used by the site team.
parts.unit_reasoning: A procedure or defined revision to one is reviewed and issued as a whole.
parts.start: need for a procedure or procedure change identified
parts.end: procedure documented and submitted for approval or use

parts.text: Implement a procedure for ongoing website revision.
parts.type_reasoning: Implementation produces a configured or established workflow for the site team.
parts.unit_reasoning: A procedure rollout is completed and handed over for routine use.
parts.start: procedure approved for implementation
parts.end: workflow established and made available to the team
parts.checked_by: site owner and staff using the procedure

notes: Implementation here means establishing the procedure, not performing each later website update.

split_reasoning: Establishing a server directory tree is one configuration activity.

parts.text: Establish a server directory tree for a website or application.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a directory structure that developers and administrators use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A directory structure for a defined site or environment is configured as a unit.
parts.start: site or environment directory requirements identified
parts.end: directory tree created and made available to the team

split_reasoning: Recommending improvements and implementing approved improvements produce different outputs.

parts.text: Recommend a website performance improvement.
parts.type_reasoning: The recommendation is a distinct proposal for a stakeholder to consider.
parts.unit_reasoning: A proposal addressing a defined performance issue is reviewed as a unit.
parts.start: performance issue or improvement opportunity identified
parts.end: recommendation communicated to the decision-maker

parts.text: Implement an approved website performance improvement.
parts.type_reasoning: Implementation produces a change to the site or its supporting systems.
parts.unit_reasoning: A defined improvement is developed and submitted as one change.
parts.start: improvement selected for implementation
parts.end: change completed and submitted for review or deployment

notes: Shares depend on the scale and approval process for improvements.

split_reasoning: The listed technical factors are contents of the same type of specification.

parts.text: Describe website specifications in clear technical detail.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a specification used by stakeholders and developers.
parts.unit_reasoning: A specification for a defined site or feature is reviewed and shared as a whole.
parts.start: requirements and technical details gathered
parts.end: specification delivered for review or implementation

split_reasoning: Continuous log monitoring is recast as the discrete problem notifications it produces.

parts.text: Identify a security problem in performance logs and notify security specialists.
parts.type_reasoning: Each identified problem produces a notification that specialists can act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: A problem notification groups the relevant log evidence for one issue.
parts.start: log entry or pattern suggesting a problem identified
parts.end: problem details sent to security specialists

notes: Routine log review that finds no problem is not a separate notification.

split_reasoning: Physical, interface, logical, and data models are alternative or combined contents of a web model or prototype.

parts.text: Create a web model or prototype for a site or application.
parts.type_reasoning: A model or prototype is a distinct artifact for stakeholders to review.
parts.unit_reasoning: A prototype or model for a defined design is shared and reviewed as a whole.
parts.start: modeling requirements or design brief received
parts.end: model or prototype delivered for review

notes: Physical models here are system models, not necessarily hands-on physical construction.

split_reasoning: Evaluating and recommending server options are stages of one selection-support activity.

parts.text: Evaluate server hardware or software and provide a recommendation.
parts.type_reasoning: The evaluation produces findings or a recommendation used in a server decision.
parts.unit_reasoning: An assessment for a defined server need is presented as a unit.
parts.work_item: one server hardware or software assessment
parts.start: server need or option identified for evaluation
parts.end: assessment or recommendation delivered to the decision-maker

split_reasoning: Test plans and procedures are prepared before execution, while test results are recorded afterward; they are different outputs.

parts.text: Document a website test plan or testing procedure.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a plan or procedure for testers to follow.
parts.unit_reasoning: A plan or procedure for a defined test scope is reviewed as a document.
parts.work_item: one documented test plan or procedure
parts.start: test scope and requirements identified
parts.end: plan or procedure shared for review or use

parts.text: Document website test results.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a results record used to assess the tested site or revision.
parts.unit_reasoning: Results for a defined test run are reported together.
parts.start: test outcomes available for documentation
parts.end: results recorded and shared with the team

notes: Shares depend on the balance of test planning and execution.

split_reasoning: Researching, documenting, rating, and selecting alternatives are stages of an architecture or technology assessment.

parts.text: Assess and document alternatives for web architecture or technologies.
parts.type_reasoning: The assessment produces a documented comparison or selection for the team.
parts.unit_reasoning: Alternatives for a defined architectural or technology decision are assessed together.
parts.work_item: one web architecture or technology alternatives assessment
parts.start: decision need and evaluation criteria identified
parts.end: comparison or selection documented and shared
parts.checked_by: architecture lead, development team, or management

split_reasoning: Server load, bandwidth, database performance, and device types are different factors recorded in the same kind of technical assessment.

parts.text: Document technical factors affecting a website or application.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a technical record used by the development or infrastructure team.
parts.unit_reasoning: A record covering a defined site, environment, or assessment period is shared as a unit.
parts.work_item: one technical factors record or report
parts.start: site or environment selected for documentation
parts.end: relevant measurements and technical factors recorded and shared

split_reasoning: Installing and configuring the HTTP server and associated operating system are parts of establishing one server environment.

parts.text: Install and configure an HTTP server and its associated operating system.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a configured server environment for the site team.
parts.unit_reasoning: A server environment is configured and handed over as a unit.
parts.start: server environment and configuration requirements assigned
parts.end: server and operating system configured and made available

notes: This codes software installation and configuration, not physical hardware installation.

split_reasoning: Interaction and sequence diagrams are closely related representations of system behavior.

parts.text: Develop a system interaction or sequence diagram.
parts.type_reasoning: The diagram is a distinct design artifact used by the development team.
parts.unit_reasoning: A diagram for a defined interaction or sequence is reviewed as a whole.
parts.work_item: one system interaction or sequence diagram
parts.start: interaction or process to model identified
parts.end: diagram completed and shared for review
